title: Field protocol v1 record event (Field to core)
description: One collected source object as a normalized source envelope: post-mapping and pre-serialization. The Field has already mapped vendor structures onto A1 vocabulary; core still owns record IDs, producer provenance, canonical bytes, key ordering, filenames, hashes, capture time, projections, and every durable write. A record is never a rendered Note and never carries a notebook path. 'change' selects an upsert of current state or an explicit authoritative deletion. Two-layer validity, illustrated by 'artifacts[].handle': this JSON Schema's pattern on 'handle' is a wire-schema well-formedness guard, and a validator run against this document alone correctly reports a traversal or absolute-path handle as not matching it. An implementation must not collapse that guard into its own DTO's field type, though: a Rust (or other language) type that enforces the same grammar during deserialization would report a hostile handle as a generic decode failure -- 'protocol.schema_invalid' -- when the pipeline stage that actually owns this rejection, and the code the transcripts pin, is the artifact-validation step that runs before any filesystem call and reports 'artifact.invalid_handle'. The reference implementation therefore carries 'handle' as an unvalidated string in its DTO and applies the grammar itself, by hand, at that later step.

object_kind.description: The capability slice this record belongs to. Must be a kind the manifest declared.

note_type.description: The primary Note type candidate. Must also equal the note_type the manifest's capability slice for this record's object_kind declares; a value that clears the A1 registry check but disagrees with the declared slice is rejected as 'record.note_type_not_declared', because 'declare before exercise' makes a slice's declared note_type a bound the Field must honour, not decoration.

properties.description: Flat property candidates keyed by A1 property names: unprefixed properties from the Note-applicable subset of the closed A1 shared registry, plus connector-prefixed properties this Field's manifest declared. A Field collects a Note, never a derived record, so registry names that exist only for a derived record -- 'confidence', 'generated_at', 'evidence_spans', 'binding_status', and the rest of that subset -- are not part of the vocabulary a record may use, even though they are registered A1 property types; core rejects one as 'record.unknown_property'. Core-owned and hoisted names are structurally excluded here. Core still validates every name, type, prefix ownership, and list semantics against the A1 registry and the declaring manifest.

body.description: Deterministically normalized source evidence for the Note body, as source text rather than a model summary. Core applies the A1 body normalization and computes the content hash; a Field never supplies a content hash.

artifacts.description: Original bytes carried by this record, in role order. Core derives the A1 'attachments' list from the members with role 'attachment', preserving this order, and the set-like 'artifacts' list from all members.

identity_anchors.description: Person, account, organization, or artifact anchors this record supplies. Anchors may relate graph entities. They are never part of the portable exact-source key and core never reconciles Notes by them.

integrity.description: Known content loss for this record, projected by core onto the A1 damage properties.

authority.description: Deletion authority. Present only on a delete. 'tombstone' requires the manifest to declare authoritative tombstones; core rejects the record otherwise. Absence of an object is never expressed as a delete record.

observed_at.description: When the Field observed the authoritative deletion. Present only on a delete.

allOf.description: An upsert carries mapped current state and no deletion authority.
A delete carries only the portable source key, its authority, and when it was observed. It never carries content, so a deletion can never be confused with an empty or partial collection result.

kind.description: 'staged' means the Field wrote the exact original bytes into the run's staging directory under 'handle'. 'digest_only' means the Field knows the artifact by digest and did not transfer bytes; core accepts it only when it already stores that digest, and otherwise rejects the record so the Field retries with bytes. 'not_retained' means the Field saw this artifact at the source and, per the retention threshold 'max_artifact_bytes' states in the collection request, declined to retain it: core stores no bytes and computes no digest, and the record is still accepted -- 'stays at source' is a policy decision, never a protocol violation.

sha256.description: The Field's declared SHA-256 over the exact original bytes. Core always computes its own digest over staged bytes and derives the A1 artifact ID from that; a disagreement rejects the record. Required for 'digest_only', where it is the only thing core has to match against bytes it already stores.

byte_length.description: For 'staged', the exact byte length core bounds the read by, at most the 536870912-byte (512 MiB) single-artifact transfer ceiling. For 'not_retained', the Field's advisory account of how large the declined bytes are, when it knows one -- deliberately unbounded here, since being over the transfer ceiling is the whole reason the Field declined to stage them, and core never reads them to check.

role.description: 'attachment' maps into the A1 role-ordered attachments list. 'original' is the source object's own bytes. Every role also appears in the set-like artifacts list.

source_filename.description: Display metadata only. Never a path component and never the stored extension: core derives both the notebook path and the canonical extension itself.

attachment_ref.description: A stable connector-namespaced upstream attachment reference (ADR 0007). Required exactly for 'not_retained' and forbidden otherwise: a staged or digest-only reference already has an A1 artifact ID, but a declined artifact has no bytes and no digest, so this is the only stable identity it carries. Core projects it onto the shared skipped_attachments Note property.
